chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Ahwal, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who is given the Hajj (quota/position) and then transfers it to another, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no objection (it is permissible).'

key_terms.الْحَجَّةَ: Hajj quota or position (often referring to the right or slot to perform pilgrimage)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to transfer one's Hajj quota to another person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of transferring one's Hajj quota (al-hajja) to another, ruling that there is no objection (la ba'sa). This reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Shia school regarding the flexibility of Hajj obligations, distinguishing between the personal duty of the individual and the administrative allocation of the pilgrimage slot. The ruling underscores the principle that the core religious act remains valid even if the logistical right is transferred, provided the recipient fulfills the ritual requirements.
